steps.title: Site Extraction
steps.short_desc: Our licensed excavation teams work alluvial and eluvial ore zones across our seven-country network, operating under active Mining Licences and rigorous supervisor oversight. Every pit is mapped, documented, and worked within the boundaries certified by the relevant national Mines & Geology authority - from the Busia goldfields of Uganda to the mineral corridors of Sierra Leone and Malawi.
steps.long_desc:
Site extraction at AfriGold Hub begins long before a shovel enters the ground. Each operating zone undergoes a formal geological assessment to map alluvial gold distribution across the deposit, identifying the highest-yield zones within our licensed acreage. Our field geologists, trained to regional mining authority standards, prepare extraction plans that balance yield optimisation with site rehabilitation requirements set by each country's environmental regulator.

In Busia, Uganda - our primary site - excavation follows the ancient Nzoia River alluvial corridor, where gold-bearing gravels have been deposited over millennia at depths of 1 to 6 metres. At our Kenya and Tanzania sites, similar alluvial formations along the Lake Victoria basin yield consistent ore grades. In Sierra Leone and South Africa, our teams work eluvial (slope-washed) deposits that require a different excavation approach, using controlled benching to expose the productive layer without disturbing the overburden excessively.

All extraction is conducted by trained, contracted crews under the direct supervision of a certified Mine Supervisor. Shift output is weighed and recorded at the pit, and a chain-of-custody log is initiated at the moment of extraction. No ore leaves the pit zone without a documented weight ticket - the first link in an unbroken documentation chain that ends at the buyer's receipt.

Post-extraction, all pit zones are progressively rehabilitated: overburden is replaced, topsoil restored, and vegetation replanting is carried out in line with each national environmental authority's closure plan requirements. In Uganda, this work is overseen by NEMA; in Kenya by the Water Resources Authority and NEMA; and in South Africa by the Department of Mineral Resources and Energy (DMRE).

steps.title: Gravity Processing
steps.short_desc: At the heart of AfriGold Hub's environmental commitment is our chemical-free gravity concentration system. Using only water, motion, and the natural density difference between gold and gangue minerals, our sluice boxes and spiral concentrators separate gold from waste with no mercury, no cyanide, and no toxic tailings - meeting and exceeding the requirements of every national environmental authority in our operating network.
steps.long_desc:
Gravity concentration is both the oldest and the cleanest method of gold recovery available to artisanal and small-scale miners. AfriGold Hub has invested heavily in modernising this technique across all seven of our country operations, deploying a staged system that consistently achieves gold recovery rates of 85–92% without a single gram of chemical input.

The process begins at the primary sluice stage, where ore-bearing gravel is fed into a high-gradient sluice box with controlled water flow. The turbulence and velocity of the water carry lighter gangue particles over the riffle bars and out of the system, while the density of gold (approximately 19.3 g/cm³, compared to 2.6–3.0 g/cm³ for common silicate gangue) causes it to settle and concentrate behind the riffles. This primary concentrate - typically 200–400 times richer in gold than the raw feed - is then passed to the spiral concentrator stage.

Our spiral concentrators, installed across all primary sites, use centrifugal and gravitational forces to further separate gold from remaining heavy and light minerals. The inner channel of the spiral collects the densest, gold-rich fraction, which is collected as secondary concentrate and passed to the final cleaning stage using a shaking table or Gemini table - producing a final concentrate clean enough for direct smelting without chemical pre-treatment.

Water used in the process is recycled through a closed settling pond system at each site, with 90–94% water recovery across our network. This dramatically reduces freshwater abstraction and ensures no process water enters natural waterways untreated. In Uganda, all water management plans are approved by the Directorate of Water Resources Management (DWRM); in Kenya by the Water Resources Authority (WRA); in South Africa by the Department of Water and Sanitation (DWS).

The absence of mercury and cyanide is not merely an environmental virtue - it is also a significant commercial advantage. Chemical processing costs (mercury, cyanide, lime, acid) are entirely eliminated, reducing our per-gram processing cost to approximately $8.40 versus $18–22 for equivalent chemical leach operations. This cost advantage directly improves investor returns.

steps.title: Smelting & Assay
steps.short_desc: Our on-site smelting furnaces convert the cleaned gravity concentrate into cast gold bars at temperatures exceeding 1,100°C. Every bar produced across our network is independently assayed for purity before release, with certificates issued to international refinery standards. Our primary Busia smelting facility produces bars consistently grading 99.5% or above - meeting London Bullion Market Association (LBMA) acceptable delivery standards.
steps.long_desc:
Smelting is the transformative stage that converts the cleaned gravity concentrate - a dark, metallic powder or fine grain - into the tangible, auditable asset of a cast gold bar. AfriGold Hub operates primary smelting furnaces at our Busia, Uganda facility and secondary smelting capabilities at our Kenya and Tanzania sites, with concentrate from Sierra Leone, Swaziland, South Africa, and Malawi consolidated and transported under secure chain-of-custody to the nearest equipped facility.

The smelting process at each facility follows a consistent protocol. Concentrate is first weighed and sampled - a fire assay sample is drawn and sent to an independent certified assay laboratory before smelting begins, establishing the expected yield and purity. The bulk concentrate is then loaded into a graphite crucible and charged into an induction furnace, which reaches operating temperature (1,064°C for pure gold, 1,100–1,150°C in practice to account for silver and base metal impurities) within 15–20 minutes.

Impurities are removed through a flux addition process - a controlled combination of borax, silica, and sodium nitrate draws base metals, sulphides, and oxides into a glass-like slag that floats above the molten gold and is skimmed off. The refined liquid metal is then poured into pre-heated graphite moulds, cast into bar form, allowed to cool under controlled conditions, and surface-finished to produce a clean, stackable bar.

Every bar is weighed on a certified balance accurate to 0.01 grams and individually marked with a unique bar serial number, pour date, site code, and weight before being presented for independent assay. In Uganda and Kenya, assay services are provided by accredited laboratories certified to KS ISO 11426 and UNBS standards respectively. In South Africa, assays are conducted to SANAS-accredited laboratory standards. The independent assay certificate accompanies every bar throughout its sale and export journey, forming a permanent part of the chain-of-custody record.

Our Busia facility has consistently produced bars grading 99.5–99.7% purity over the past three years of operation. Each consignment - typically 15–20 bars totalling 250–280 kg - is photographed, weighed, assay-certified, and placed in sealed, tamper-evident packaging before transfer to the licensed buyer.

steps.title: Sale & Distribution
steps.short_desc: Finished gold bars are sold exclusively through government-licensed precious metals buyers in each operating country, with full royalty declarations, export documentation, and KRA/URA/TMGA receipts issued per transaction. Proceeds are transferred to the AfriGold Hub operating account within 48 hours of delivery, with investor distributions processed within 10 business days of month-end - every month, without exception.
steps.long_desc:
The sale and distribution stage is where every gram of production becomes investor return - and where AfriGold Hub's commitment to full transparency is most directly tested. We operate a strictly regulated, fully documented sale process across all seven countries, working only with buyers who hold valid precious metals dealer licences from the relevant national revenue or mining authority.

In Uganda - our primary market - gold is sold to Uganda Revenue Authority (URA)-registered precious metals dealers operating under licences issued by the Directorate of Geological Survey and Mines (DGSM). Each transaction is accompanied by a formal sale agreement, a KYC-verified buyer certificate, the bar's independent assay certificate, and a URA-receipted royalty declaration (Uganda's mineral royalty is currently 3% of gross value for artisanal gold). The physical handover is documented with bar serial numbers, weights, and buyer acknowledgment - and both parties retain original copies.

In Kenya, sales proceed through KRA-registered dealers with Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) foreign exchange approval for international settlement. In Tanzania, all gold sales are reported to the Tanzania Minerals Audit Agency (TMAA) and documented under TANSORT (Tanzania Minerals Sorting and Smelting Company) protocols. South African consignments are handled through SARS-registered dealers under DMRE oversight, while Sierra Leone, Swaziland, and Malawi sales follow the respective national mining ministry dealer registration requirements.

All sale proceeds are received into the AfriGold Hub operating account - a joint account accessible to Strategic and Anchor tier partners - within 48 hours of physical delivery and buyer confirmation. Monthly revenue is reconciled against production records, assay certificates, and buyer receipts by our CFO and an external accountant, producing the monthly audited P&L that goes to all investment partners within 10 business days of month-end.

Investor distributions are transferred via SWIFT international bank transfer (USD) or mobile money (for Africa-based partners who prefer it) on a fixed schedule - the 15th of each month for the prior month's production. Late payment, in our history, has never occurred. The entire sale and distribution process - from bar handover to investor payment - is documented in our monthly investor pack: a 6-page PDF that includes the sale receipts, assay certificates, bank statement excerpt, P&L, and distribution breakdown by partner tier.

items.q: Is AfriGold Hub a licensed mining operation?
items.a: Yes. We operate under a valid Primary Mining Licence (PML) issued under Africa's Mining Act 2010. All environmental and safety certifications are current and available for investor review upon request.

items.q: How are investor returns calculated and distributed?
items.a: Returns are calculated monthly based on verified gold sales receipts. Net profit after operational costs is distributed to investors in proportion to their equity tier. Payments are made via bank transfer within 10 business days of month-end reconciliation.

All partnerships are governed by a formal investment agreement. Capital is held in an escrow-style joint account. Strategic and Anchor partners have direct visibility into the bank account. Monthly audited reports are provided without exception.

items.q: Why is gravity concentration better than chemical processing?
items.a: Gravity concentration uses no mercury or cyanide, significantly lowering operational costs and eliminating environmental liability. It is fully NEMC-compliant and aligns with Africa's move to phase out mercury in artisanal mining.

items.q: What is the minimum investment commitment period?
items.a: The minimum commitment is three months, which also aligns with the projected capital payback window. After the initial term, partners may roll over, exit, or renegotiate their tier with 30 days' notice.
